::: {.accroche}
I build calculation and projection models for organisations that need to **cost a reform, simulate entitlements or anticipate spending**. My work consists in translating rules — legislation, collective agreements, rate schedules — into reliable, tested code, and turning it into figures people can decide on.
:::

I took part in creating the open-source software [OpenFisca](https://openfisca.org/en/), which powers French public benefit simulators such as *Mes droits sociaux* and *1jeune1solution*. I spent ten years as an economist at the [Institut des politiques publiques](https://www.ipp.eu/en/), then at the French National Assembly (LexImpact), before working as a consultant, notably for the World Bank.

## What I do

- **Simulators and calculation engines** — benefits, entitlements, social contributions, taxes, bonuses: complex rules turned into a tested, documented engine.
- **Costing and impact assessment** — budgetary cost of a measure, effects of a change in rates or thresholds, distributional analysis, scenario comparison.
- **Projections** — payroll and headcount, spending, pension or insurance schemes, populations.
- **Data and training** — administrative and survey data, web simulation apps, Python training for your teams.

## Background

- **2014–2024** — Economist, Institut des politiques publiques: microsimulation of taxes, benefits and pensions (OpenFisca France, TAXIPP models), costing of budget bills, long-term care projections, fiscal incidence in West Africa.
- **2023** — Economist, French National Assembly (LexImpact).
- **2009–2014** — Economist, France Stratégie (Prime Minister's policy office): creation of OpenFisca.
- **2001–2008** — Physical oceanographer: assistant professor (Université de Bretagne Occidentale), postdoctoral fellow (Woods Hole, CNRS).
- **Education** — MSc in Economics (Paris School of Economics), PhD in Physics (Université Paris VI – ENS).
